consumerDefects.title: Preserve browser occurrence identity across repeated evaluate results
evidence: observation-browser.js:59-64 and149-159 repeatedly return the existing window.__nsLifecycleRecorderError.

Playwright coreBundle.js:12028-12030 creates a new deserialization reference map per result; :12079-12083 creates a new object for an object value. JSHandle/Frame evaluate returns parseResult for each response at :57800-57801 and60411-60412.
error-ledger.js:84-102 only deduplicates matching object references and WeakMap keys; it has no browser occurrence-domain/order key, and materializeEnvelope at :50-69 does not retain obsOrder.
evidence.js:101-105 directly forwards to that ledger. collectLivePageDiagnostics at live-evidence.js:71-74 performs a later readPassiveEvents using the same sink.
consumerDefects.mechanism: After an initial cursor/correlated/extraction read forwards a retained recorder failure, later live/passive collection can forward that same browser occurrence again. Separate evaluate responses reconstruct distinct envelope objects, so the ledger creates another normalized Error and another occurrence/order despite identical document-local obsOrder. Same-call Set deduplication and Node Error reference deduplication cannot repair this boundary. This is a static consumer trace, not a measured run or invented output.
consumerDefects.requiredRepairBoundary: Preserve internal occurrence identity across browser serialization and Node ingestion using the actual document/timeOrigin namespace and a genuine observation-site occurrence witness. Do not deduplicate unrelated Node Errors or unrelated documents solely by numeric order; do not change public signatures.

consumerDefects.title: Retain every relevant sibling on matched-packet rejection paths
evidence: observation.js:107 selects a matched packet and :113-118 normalizes using that packet before checking current-node agreement.
observation-errors.js:52-55 processes only the supplied packet; the all-candidate loop is reachable only in the else branch.
observation-domain.js:43-57 supplies connected-root/domain rejection after this normalization gate.
consumerDefects.mechanism: If a sequence-eligible packet exactly matches the cursor, additional eligible packets contain genuine getter failures, and the current root is subsequently found disconnected or another outer extraction condition rejects, the additional packets are never normalized. The raw candidate array remains staged, but the rejection terminates the path before their genuine sibling errors reach the ledger. Processing all candidates on the no-match branch fixes only part of the retained rejection-path obligation.
consumerDefects.requiredRepairBoundary: Keep exact successful packet acceptance unchanged; ensure every relevant cursor-eligible packet's genuine siblings are normalized before an outer rejection can terminate extraction.

consumerDefects.title: Do not probe configured keyboard conditions by invoking them
evidence: navigation.js:76 calls priorCondition({target: active}) before the actual keyboard.press at :143.
reveal-lifecycle.js:75-82 delegates its wrapper to an arbitrary priorCondition.
keyboard.js:146 supplies the real KeyboardEvent to production condition dispatch.
consumerDefects.mechanism: The diagnostic read executes the configured condition callback once with an incomplete synthetic event before production executes it for the real key. A key-dependent condition does not receive the pressed key/keyCode/modifiers during this probe; a condition with effects is executed during observation. This is a retained no-probing contract violation and remaining eligibility mismatch, not a claim that the condition call was newly introduced in Correction11.
consumerDefects.requiredRepairBoundary: Use read-only owner-backed discriminators; do not call condition or binding callbacks to discover effects, force focus, or mutate keyboard policy.

observationOrderDomainAnalysis.conclusion: The normalization consumer has no explicit defense against mixing numeric observation orders from different document/timeOrigin domains. Ordinary intact initialization creates a document-local packet/error collection, and the read source alone does not establish that an ordinary untampered extraction batch naturally mixes documents. Therefore no observed cross-document ordering result or independent mixed-document defect is fabricated. Heterogeneous/corrupted packet inputs cannot be certified as meaningfully globally sortable, and action-packet replacement remains the excluded NF-A4 boundary.

recordedExcludedScopeCandidateVerbatim.consumerVisibleMechanism: evaluateActionCandidates returns candidates from the public, replaceable window.__nsRecordedPackets (:146-147). storeHealth (:148) checks only the lifecycle store. In-place mutation of an original packet is detected, because that packet object is also the retained native-action detail. Replacing the array, or replacing an element with a forged object, leaves the retained and private stores untouched, so health stays true. extractActionBracket (observation.js:107-131) then builds the action bracket from the forged packet: rootEventsBefore/After, stateAfter and tCapture/tBubble, which witness.js:44-63 adopts as the Start baseline. This is the same public-store replacement model as N07-04, applied to the packet store.
